clue.text: Feminine, ash-blonde, old, mad — but family

indicators.note: something mad is crazed and disordered, so these letters are thrown into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A list of descriptions of a crazy old blonde woman, who nonetheless is related to you.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram takes F plus ASHBLONDE plus OLD, thirteen letters in all.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means one's own relatives, kin by birth.

clue.text: Letters offering a good job

definitions.meaning: mail sent by the faster, dearer Royal Mail service
a top-quality appointment, taking the second word as a position

explanation.surface: Correspondence presenting someone with an attractive employment opportunity.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain, mail can be sent at a faster first-class rate; the second sense reads 'post' as a job.
explanation.definitionFit: Letters sent at the premium Royal Mail rate, and also an excellent position or appointment.

clue.text: Do better in former prison accommodation, being cut off

parts.note: ex- is the prefix meaning former

indicators.note: a word cut off loses its tail, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a prisoner is kept in a cell

explanation.surface: An improvement in a disused jail's quarters, now isolated from the outside world.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being cut off' trims the final L from CELL.
explanation.definitionFit: To surpass or outshine others is to do better than them.

clue.text: Complete skill shown by hospital transport vehicle

parts.note: H is the map and sign abbreviation for hospital
over means finished, completed
craft means skill or art

explanation.surface: A medical transport vehicle displaying great expertise.
explanation.definitionFit: It is an air-cushion vehicle used to carry passengers over land and sea.

clue.text: Swimmer's nervous anticipation returned when help arrived laughing, initially

definitions.note: Swimmer's here is 'swimmer is', the definition plus a link

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of each of the seven words before it

parts.words: nervous anticipation returned when help arrived laughing

explanation.surface: A swimmer felt anxious waiting until help came, laughing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' is only a word giving its initial, not a reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: This Arctic whale, with its long tusk, is a marine swimmer.

clue.text: Fast traveller that no one welcomes

definitions.text: Fast traveller that no one welcomes

parts.words: Fast traveller that no one welcomes
parts.note: plays on the saying that unwelcome tidings travel fast

explanation.surface: A speedy voyager whom nobody is pleased to see.
explanation.walkthrough: The proverb 'ill tidings travel fast' makes the unwelcome message a quick traveller.
explanation.definitionFit: Unwelcome tidings are proverbially quick to spread, and no one is glad to receive them.

clue.text: Dearie me! Top's come off chicken enclosures

indicators.note: in a down clue the top is the first letter, which is removed

parts.note: chickens are kept in coops

explanation.surface: An exclamation of dismay as the roofs blow off the hen houses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top's come off' drops the C at the head of COOPS.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are mild exclamations of dismay at a small mishap.

clue.text: Germany? First to accept coach's seizure ordered by court

parts.note: D is the international vehicle code for Germany

indicators.note: IST accepts the coach by taking it inside

parts.note: 1ST, written IST, is first
to coach is to train; the 's is 'is', a link

explanation.surface: A query about Germany and a coach having goods seized by legal order.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First' is written as 1ST with the digit read as the letter I; 'to accept' means it takes the coach inside itself.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the legal seizure of goods, typically to force payment of a debt.

clue.text: A jacket like this needs new blue beret, as odd

indicators.note: new signals the letters are made into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: Fashion advice: this jacket demands a fresh blue beret, however strange that looks.
explanation.definitionFit: Describes a jacket whose front overlaps with two rows of buttons.

clue.text: Got back with insurance, after evacuating Rome

indicators.note: after places the insurance piece behind the emptied city
evacuating empties the word of its inner letters, leaving its ends

parts.note: being insured means being covered

explanation.surface: Someone recouped losses through an insurance policy after fleeing Rome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'evacuating Rome' leaves RE, its outer letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To regain or retrieve something is to have got it back.

clue.text: Nuisance taking first portion of onion sauce

parts.note: a pest is an annoying person

indicators.note: the first portion of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: An irritating person helping themselves to the first serving of onion sauce.
explanation.definitionFit: A basil, pine nut and cheese sauce from Genoa, usually served with pasta.

clue.text: Tradesman's pound deposited in bank

definitions.note: Tradesman's is 'tradesman is', the definition plus a link

indicators.note: deposited in places the pound inside the bank

parts.note: a tier is a row or bank, as of seats
L (from Latin libra) is the abbreviation for pound

explanation.surface: A tradesman puts his money into the bank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bank' is not a financial bank but a tier, a row.
explanation.definitionFit: A tradesman who lays tiles on roofs, walls or floors.

clue.text: Works on garden dwellings with no end of charm

indicators.note: with no means the following letter is removed

parts.note: homes are dwellings

indicators.note: end of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: Someone tends the garden at houses lacking any appeal.
explanation.walkthrough: The end of 'charm' is M, removed from HOMES.
explanation.definitionFit: To dig and weed with a garden tool is to work on a garden; verb in third person.

clue.text: Dull brown flatfish swimming across river

indicators.note: the fish swims across, spanning the river letter so that it sits inside

parts.note: a dab is a small flatfish

explanation.surface: A dull-coloured flatfish swims over a river.
explanation.definitionFit: A dull, light brownish colour, also meaning dreary.

clue.text: Many labels must be wrong, of course

indicators.note: letters that are wrong need putting right in another order

explanation.surface: Naturally, a lot of the labels are bound to be mistaken.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are phrases of emphatic agreement or permission, certainly.

clue.text: Large ugly tear with a line on the side

parts.note: L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

indicators.note: ugly suggests the letters are distorted into a different shape

explanation.surface: A big nasty rip with a line down the side.
explanation.definitionFit: Lateral means relating to or situated at the side.

clue.text: Distressing illusion, mostly about gold rug

indicators.note: about means going around the other pieces
mostly means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a trick can be an illusion, as an optical trick
AU is the chemical symbol for gold
a mat is a small rug

explanation.surface: A distressing optical illusion involving a mostly golden rug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' trims TRICK to TRIC, which goes 'about' AU and MAT.
explanation.definitionFit: Something causing severe emotional shock is deeply upsetting.

clue.text: Left home, absorbed by island's horizon

indicators.note: absorbed by puts these pieces inside the island

parts.note: Skye is a Scottish island; the 's is a link
to be in is to be at home

explanation.surface: Someone departs home to be taken in by an island's horizon.
explanation.definitionFit: The outline where land or buildings meet the sky, the visible horizon.

clue.text: Supplied personnel and stopped replacing students with females

indicators.note: replacing means exchanging one pair of letters for another

parts.note: a stalled engine has stopped
L is a learner, so two learners make students
F is the abbreviation for female, doubled for females

explanation.surface: A school was given staff, and stopped swapping its students for women.
explanation.walkthrough: In STALLED the LL (learner drivers in Britain display an L plate) becomes FF.
explanation.definitionFit: To man a business is to provide it with workers.

clue.text: A long time after mother's court award

indicators.note: after puts the long time behind the mother

parts.note: a dam is an animal's mother; the 's is a link
ages is a long time

explanation.surface: A mother's lengthy wait before a court compensation award.
explanation.definitionFit: Money awarded by a court as compensation for loss or injury.

clue.text: Lobster served as this on a bed?

indicators.note: food is served after being dressed, here rearranged into a new form

explanation.surface: A lobster presented on a bed of lettuce.
explanation.walkthrough: In the kitchen a lobster is served on a bed of leaves; here the bed is for sleeping.
explanation.definitionFit: A long, firm pillow placed across the head of a bed.

clue.text: The tedium of showing embarrassment during sudden prosperity?

indicators.note: during places the blushing piece inside the prosperity

parts.note: an economic boom is a time of sudden prosperity
a red face shows embarrassment

explanation.surface: Musing on why a boom time might feel dull and embarrassing.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean the weariness felt from dullness or lack of interest.

clue.text: Question source of water

definitions.meaning: to interrogate someone persistently for information
a device drawing water up from a well

explanation.surface: Asking where water comes from.
explanation.definitionFit: To grill someone for information, and a device raising water from a well.

clue.text: Title held by the Mirror

indicators.note: held by means the letters are contained within the following words

explanation.surface: A title owned by a newspaper, the Mirror.
explanation.walkthrough: The Mirror is a British tabloid newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the title of a Muslim ruler or commander.

clue.text: Mother gets fellow — one with a criminal family

parts.note: ma is mother
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Mum takes up with a man who belongs to a gangster clan.
explanation.definitionFit: A secret organised crime syndicate, whose units are known as families.

clue.text: Father always stands for this Scandinavian beauty

parts.note: Fr is the abbreviation for Father, a priest

indicators.note: in a down clue, standing means rising up, so the word is read bottom to top

parts.note: aye is an old word for always

explanation.surface: A father holding out for a beautiful Scandinavian woman.
explanation.definitionFit: The Norse goddess of love and beauty.

clue.text: Refuse with contempt, lacking new incentive

indicators.note: lacking means the letter is removed

parts.note: to spurn is to reject scornfully

explanation.surface: Disdainfully rejecting something that offers no fresh motivation.
explanation.definitionFit: A goad or stimulus to action, as a rider's goad urges a horse on.

clue.text: Found television well-informed

parts.note: a TV set
being up on a subject means knowing it well

explanation.surface: Discovered that the TV is knowledgeable.
explanation.definitionFit: To found a company is to establish or create it.

clue.text: Progress with daughter meeting standard set by hospital department sponsor

parts.note: to go is to proceed or progress
par is the standard or norm
ENT is ear, nose and throat

explanation.surface: A daughter's progress measured against the standards of a hospital department's sponsor.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who sponsors a child at baptism, promising religious guidance.

clue.text: Festive wit's annual missive?

parts.note: the festive season is Christmas
a card is a wit or joker; the 's is a link

explanation.surface: A joker's yearly letter sent at the festive season.
explanation.walkthrough: 'card' is an old-fashioned word for a joker, an amusing person.
explanation.definitionFit: A greeting sent once a year at the festive season; the question mark flags the loose definition.
